citation.title: The behaviour of fast ions in tokamak experiments

topic: A review of fast-ion origin, slowing-down, confinement and fast-ion-driven instabilities in tokamaks from 1970 to 1992.
own_question: How do fast ions from beams, RF heating and fusion reactions behave, and what does that imply for alpha particles?
actual_method_and_evidence: Literature review covering neutral particle analysers, neutron, fusion-product and gamma diagnostics. It compares these measurements with Coulomb, Stix, orbit and ripple theory. The review has no treatment of carbon-impurity CES pedestal temperature, BES or ECEI nowcasting, or KSTAR.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. The paper does not address CES report timing or causal estimation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not use this paper to support any claim about CES, BES, ECEI or KSTAR pedestal behaviour.
Do not cite its discussion of charge-exchange neutral analysers as evidence about CES impurity-temperature labels.
Do not infer machine-learning or real-time relevance from this paper.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The paper concerns the physics of suprathermal ions. Its use of charge-exchange neutral particle analysis is a different diagnostic from charge-exchange spectroscopy, and nothing in it bears on causal nowcasting of impurity CES temperature at the pedestal top.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
